chapter: Chez Florence, the Hot Club and Django
title: Panassie at the Ambassador: 'Why don't you play like Mezzrow?'
summary: Hugues Panassie visited Briggs backstage while he played with Sissle, asked why he did not play like Mezz Mezzrow, and Sissle told him to go and hear Mezzrow.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay, well, then let's go -- let's talk about the Hot Club of France, because you were telling me earlier some things about that, that I hadn't known before, --
About how that had gotten started.
Yes, yes. Well, it started through, as I told you, through my friend, --
Panassie. We -- as a matter of fact, I met Panassie while I was with Sissle's orchestra at the Ambassador as he came to tea dance one day, and came backstage to see me.
He must have been just a kid then?
Well, yes. Oh, he might have been around 21, 22.
And he came backstage and saw me, and he ----Tommy Ladnier was not with the orchestra yet.
He came back and he said, "Why don't you play like that, like our boy --"
I mean, he wasn't in his corner, yet.
No, no. I know a good clarinet player, Mezzrow.

said, 'Why don't you play like Mezzrow?' I said, 'Well, look,' I said, 'You go to Mr. Sissle and you tell Mr. Sissle, 'Why don't he play like Mezzrow.'" He went up to Sissle, he said, 'You don't play real jazz.' He spoke little English. 'Why don't you play like Mezzrow?' So, Sissle said, 'Well, look, all you go to do is to go where Mezzrow is playing. That's all, just go where Mezzrow is playing.' He wasn't in France then.
No, he had just heard his -- that lousy, one of his lousy recordings. That's all we heard when we went to Panassie's place.
And he had a clarinet. He tried to play the clarinet, imitation --
Somebody's going to burn me up when they hear.
You were talking about Jean Brashear.

Hugues financed the -- as I said, he came to the Ambassadors, and he wanted, he asked me, "Why don't you play like Mezzrow," so I told him to see Noble and ask Noble that question. So, he went and asked Noble. He said, "Why don't you all play like Mezzrow?" So, Sissle, he said, "Why don't you go and see, if you want to hear someone play like Mezzrow, go and listen to Mezzrow yourself." (Laughter).
Okay, I guess we're all set. That seems to be coming through fine.
